text: Rust rejects two live mutable references to the same value so mutation stays exclusive: only one reference can change the value while it is borrowed. That rule blocks data races and the aliasing bugs that follow from mutating a value through one reference while another still uses it, such as iterator invalidation and use-after-free.
thought:
Rust forbids two mutable references to the same value because that would allow data races and memory corruption. The borrow checker prevents use-after-free, double-free, and buffer overflow bugs.

The specific bug class is mutable aliasing. It enables iterator invalidation and concurrent data races.
